theme: Agent 在採取行動前，哪些控制閘門會失效
notes: The official listing batch is used as the publication window because arXiv does not announce new submissions on Friday or Saturday and submission timestamps can differ from announcement dates.
Thirty topical candidates were abstract-screened. Full method, experiment, baseline, and limitation checks were completed for all three selected papers.
The previous local article selection was replaced because two papers had been described from abstract-level evidence under the earlier standard.

candidates.title: Calibrated Enough to Know, Not Calibrated to Act
credibilityEvidence: Sections 4-5: 12-model preregistered evaluation separates answerability calibration from action commitment.
Results: commitment rises from 6.5% to 54.0% across evidence escalation; real-rich and fully fabricated panels are equivalent within the prespecified +/-5 percentage-point margin.
Limitations: the effect is heterogeneous and concentrated in three models from one developer; weather is a weak instrument and hosted serving settings are uncontrolled.
Public code, cached outputs, preregistration, and Zenodo artifacts are linked from the paper.
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Preregistered equivalence tests, interventions, heterogeneous model results, and explicit limitations support the narrow action-commitment claim, but not a universal frontier-model claim.
reproducibilityEvidence: Public GitHub repository with code, preregistration, and cached outputs
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: The article limits its conclusion to evidence presentation increasing action commitment in the tested settings.
candidates.primaryLimitation: The susceptibility effect is concentrated in three models from one developer.
candidates.presentationReason: The preregistered hypotheses, evidence conditions, statistical equivalence test, model heterogeneity, interventions, and limitations are separated and traceable.
candidates.reason: Shows that evidence-shaped context can move action commitment without improving knowledge, with unusually explicit heterogeneity and reproducibility disclosures.

candidates.title: When Tool Outputs Become Commands: Separating Action Induction from Runtime Authorization in Tool-Augmented LLM Agents
credibilityEvidence: Method: SARA separates action induction from execution authorization and prevents action-origin laundering through persistent provenance state.
Tables 1-3: evaluated on 3,528 AgentDojo and 5,202 AgentDyn attack instances plus benign tasks against eight named defenses.
Results: GPT-4o-mini ASR falls from 15.79% to 0.06% on AgentDojo and 16.07% to 0.17% on AgentDyn; cross-backbone residuals and ablations are reported.
Limitations and cost: not a formal guarantee, scoped to tool-based indirect prompt injection, and total input is 1.91x to 2.21x the agent-only baseline.
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Two benchmark suites, eight defense comparisons, cross-backbone checks, utility measurements, and ablations support the runtime-authorization claim without establishing a formal guarantee.
reproducibilityEvidence: Algorithms, benchmark datasets, configurations, and ablation definitions are described
A complete public implementation and cached outputs were not confirmed
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: The evidence supports the engineering value of separating action induction from execution authorization under the stated trust assumptions.
candidates.primaryLimitation: The evaluation covers tool-based indirect prompt injection and assumes trusted users, schemas, runtimes, and executors.
candidates.presentationReason: The authorization model, persistent provenance state, threat assumptions, benchmark protocol, baseline comparisons, ablations, and token costs are stated distinctly.
candidates.reason: Provides a concrete runtime authorization architecture, broad attack evaluation, fair baseline comparison, and visible utility and token costs.

candidates.title: Safety Does Not Compose: Non-Decaying Loop State for Autonomous LLM Agents
credibilityEvidence: Theory: formal indistinguishability argument explains why trajectory-scoped monitors cannot detect fragmented loop attacks without matching false positives.
Track B: 1,000 attack episodes per configuration on a 200-task pool; the full controller reports 0.1% ASR versus 88.4%-97.6% for weakened variants, with 96.9% clean goal completion.
Retention test: a non-decaying latch stays at 0% ASR across waiting intervals while geometric decay returns to 97% by d=2.
Limitation: one frozen model-role assignment and one execution seed on structured synthetic attacks; no multi-seed or multi-model-role replication.
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Formal analysis and targeted ablations support the temporal-state failure mechanism, while one frozen role configuration and one execution seed do not establish broad empirical generality.
reproducibilityEvidence: The paper describes supplementary controller components, attack suites, a report generator, deterministic seeds, and cached model calls
An independent public repository was not confirmed
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Confidence is higher in the non-decaying-state design warning than in the reported attack-rate magnitude across other systems.
candidates.primaryLimitation: One frozen model-role configuration, one execution seed, and structured synthetic attacks.
candidates.presentationReason: The formal claim, controller components, attack tracks, ablations, fixed model-role protocol, and availability limitation are explicit even though empirical generality is narrow.
candidates.reason: The theory and ablations expose a temporal-state design failure, but the empirical generality is still narrow enough to require conditional language.

candidates.title: WikiSkill
candidates.reason: Relevant skill-learning system, but less urgent than the three control-gate failures after abstract screening.

candidates.title: RedEvoAgent
candidates.reason: Promising evolving red-team agent; retained for a security-focused batch rather than promoted without full-text review.

candidates.title: Persona-Execution Separation
candidates.reason: Useful architecture idea, but abstract evidence did not outrank the selected runtime-control work.

candidates.title: INTENT-AS-A-TOOL
candidates.reason: Intent mediation is relevant, but the direction overlaps with stronger authorization evidence in SARA.

candidates.title: One Model, Many Minds
candidates.reason: Multi-agent role diversity is interesting, but practical and evidence boundaries need full-text review.

candidates.title: BTS-AgentBench
candidates.reason: Benchmark contribution is directly relevant but did not form the strongest same-day editorial direction.

candidates.title: Verify Smarter: HarnessLens
candidates.reason: Verification efficiency is promising; numerical claims require a separate full-text credibility pass.

candidates.title: What Makes Good Agentic Data
candidates.reason: Potentially useful data-selection result, but outside today's runtime safety theme.

candidates.title: Contract-Centered Runtime
candidates.reason: Contracts align with today's theme, but SARA and LoopHarness offered stronger inspectable evidence for the available slots.

candidates.title: FaulT-Bench
candidates.reason: Fault-tolerance evaluation is valuable but needs full benchmark construction review before selection.

candidates.title: ASIL
candidates.reason: Relevant system work, but abstract screening did not establish a direction-changing result.

candidates.title: GraphMemix
candidates.reason: Previously selected from abstract-level evidence; removed until its claimed Pareto improvement receives a full-text verification pass.

candidates.title: Collaborative Vector Memory
candidates.reason: Memory coordination is relevant but not more urgent than the selected safety boundary results.

candidates.title: PLCBench
candidates.reason: Benchmark may matter to coding agents, but requires task-validity and leakage review.

candidates.title: BekchiAI
candidates.reason: Application-specific agent system with lower cross-reader direction value.

candidates.title: Confidence-Gated Retrieval
candidates.reason: Useful retrieval gating idea, but it did not outrank the more general action-calibration finding.

candidates.title: Decoupling Planning and Control
candidates.reason: Architecturally relevant, though its evidence and distinction from existing planning-control splits need full review.

candidates.title: Experimental Fidelity: ABE-Ralph
candidates.reason: Evaluation fidelity is important, but benchmark validity cannot be accepted from the abstract alone.

candidates.title: Daydreaming Skill Theft
candidates.reason: Novel attack surface, reserved for a full security evidence pass.

candidates.title: Five Primitives for Runtime Governance
candidates.reason: Governance primitives fit the theme, but inspectable empirical support was weaker than the selected papers at screening time.

candidates.title: Adaptive Reasoning in Agentic AI
candidates.reason: Broad direction paper with less concrete immediate decision value.

candidates.title: KnownLieBench
candidates.reason: Deception evaluation is relevant, but requires construction and contamination review before promotion.

candidates.title: MemToC
candidates.reason: Memory method is in scope but did not produce the strongest new direction today.

candidates.title: SKILL.state
candidates.reason: Stateful skill management is promising; full method and baseline review remains necessary.

candidates.title: CTF-ABACUS
candidates.reason: Trace provenance for security agents is relevant but application-specific and not fully reviewed.

candidates.title: Agent Mesh
candidates.reason: Multi-agent infrastructure has practical value, but novelty and evidence require full-text assessment.

candidates.title: Same Model, Different Harness
candidates.reason: Harness sensitivity is highly relevant; retained for a dedicated evaluation batch rather than squeezed into today's safety theme.
